subject.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers

question: Should remaining volatile below-boundary additions move into the canonical absolute-tail runtime-context mechanism, or should DeepSeek receive this broad public system-to-user compatibility mode?
rationale: Current main establishes tail placement as the cache-stable architecture for inbound metadata, while this PR adds a provider-specific config/default and rewrites a broader instruction class; source inspection and existing proof cannot safely choose that permanent contract.

options.title: Extend typed tail context
options.body: Classify each remaining below-boundary addition and move only proven per-turn volatile context to the absolute-tail carrier, preserving system authority.

options.title: Accept broad DeepSeek mode
options.body: Keep the public option and automatic default only after differential live counters and multi-step role-semantics proof.

options.title: Pause pending isolation
options.body: Keep the canonical issue and candidates open until a latest-main reproduction identifies which remaining addition still breaks DeepSeek caching.

recommendation.title: Extend typed tail context
recommendation.body: Classify each remaining below-boundary addition and move only proven per-turn volatile context to the absolute-tail carrier, preserving system authority.
